decisions.choice: un seul pain, as in verse 16
decisions.reason: The English says "loaf" here because "one bread" is not natural English. French "un pain" is itself a loaf, so French keeps the same word as in verse 16 and the link between the bread that is broken and the one loaf stays visible.

decisions.choice: pan
decisions.reason: Spanish "pan" names a loaf as well as bread, so one word serves where the English says "loaf".

decisions.choice: "한 몸" for the church as one body at every level, through chapter 12
decisions.reason: The same word "몸" serves Christ's body given in death (verse 16) and the church as his body, so the link Paul draws can be seen.

source.text: βλέπετε τὸν Ἰσραὴλ κατὰ σάρκα· οὐχ οἱ ἐσθίοντες τὰς θυσίας κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου εἰσίν;

records.literal_gloss: Look at the Israel according to flesh; not those eating the sacrifices sharers of the altar are?

en.L: Look at Israel according to flesh: those who eat the sacrifices, are they not sharers in the altar?
en.B: Look at Israel, the nation by human descent. Do not the people who eat from the sacrifices share in the altar?
en.R: Think about the people of Israel. When they eat meat from the animals offered on the altar, they are taking part in the worship offered there.

fr.L: Regardez Israël selon la chair : ceux qui mangent les sacrifices ne participent-ils pas à l’autel ?
fr.B: Regardez Israël selon la chair, le peuple issu d’une même descendance. Ceux qui mangent des sacrifices n’ont-ils pas part à l’autel ?
fr.R: Pensez au peuple d’Israël. Quand les Israélites mangent la viande des animaux offerts sur l’autel, ils participent au culte qu’on y rend.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a Israel según la carne: los que comen los sacrificios, ¿no son partícipes del altar?
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a Israel, el pueblo por descendencia humana. ¿No participan del altar los que comen de los sacrificios?
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en el pueblo de Israel. Cuando comen la carne de los animales ofrecidos sobre el altar, están tomando parte en la adoración que allí se ofrece.

sw.L: Tazameni Israeli kwa kadiri ya mwili: je, wale wanaokula dhabihu si washiriki wa madhabahu?
sw.B: Tazameni Israeli, taifa kwa uzao wa kibinadamu. Je, wale wanaokula sehemu ya dhabihu hawashiriki madhabahu?
sw.R: Fikirini juu ya watu wa Israeli. Wanapokula nyama ya wanyama waliotolewa sadaka juu ya madhabahu, wanashiriki katika ibada inayotolewa pale.

vi.L: Hãy xem dân Y-sơ-ra-ên theo xác thịt: những người ăn các sinh tế há chẳng phải là những người dự phần với bàn thờ sao?
vi.B: Hãy nhìn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, là dân tộc theo dòng dõi con người. Chẳng phải những người ăn của sinh tế được dự phần với bàn thờ sao?
vi.R: Hãy nghĩ đến dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Khi họ ăn thịt các con vật đã được dâng trên bàn thờ, là họ đang tham dự vào sự thờ phượng được dâng lên ở đó.

ko.L: 육신을 따른 이스라엘을 보십시오. 제물을 먹는 사람들은 제단에 참여하는 사람들이 아닙니까?
ko.B: 혈통으로 난 이스라엘 백성을 보십시오. 제물을 먹는 사람들은 제단에 함께 참여하는 사람들이 아닙니까?
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성을 생각해 보십시오. 그들은 제단에 바친 짐승의 고기를 먹을 때 그 제단에서 드리는 예배에 함께 참여하는 것입니다.

decisions.choice: Israel according to the flesh: the people of Israel by physical descent, in their ordinary worship
alternatives: unfaithful Israel, such as those who worshiped the golden calf
decisions.reason: κατὰ σάρκα distinguishes the nation by birth from the wider people of God in Christ (compare Romans 9:3-8). Paul is not condemning Israel's sacrifices here; he uses them to show what eating a sacrifice means.

decisions.choice: those who eat the sacrifices: worshipers and priests who ate part of the offered animal
decisions.reason: In some of Israel's offerings part of the animal was burned on the altar and the rest eaten by the priests and the worshipers (Leviticus 7:11-18; Deuteronomy 12:17-18; compare 9:13).

decisions.choice: sharers in the altar: partners in the worship offered at the altar, and so with the God to whom it is offered
alternatives: sharing only the food from the altar
decisions.reason: κοινωνοὶ is a partner, someone who shares with others. The altar stands for the God worshiped there. The same word is used of demons in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the nation by human descent
decisions.reason: As the terms doc does for σάρξ elsewhere, Balanced gives the sense.

decisions.choice: When they eat meat from the animals offered on the altar, they are taking part in the worship offered there
decisions.reason: Readable explains the sacrifices (m2) and what sharing in the altar means (m3), and turns the question into the statement it expects.

decisions.choice: Israël selon la chair, le peuple issu d'une même descendance (B)
alternatives: Israël, la nation par la descendance humaine
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "la chair" at Literal and Balanced, and here it reads naturally in French; Balanced adds what it means, the people by physical descent (m1), where the English Balanced gives only the sense.

decisions.choice: "육신을 따른" (L); "혈통으로 난" (B)
decisions.reason: The words of Romans 9:3 (L, B) for Israel by physical descent.

source.text: τί οὖν φημι;

records.literal_gloss: What then do I say?

en.L: What then am I saying?
en.B: What am I saying, then?
en.R: What do I mean by this?

fr.L: Que dis-je donc ?
fr.B: Que suis-je donc en train de dire ?
fr.R: Qu’est-ce que je veux dire par là ?

es.L: ¿Qué digo, entonces?
es.B: ¿Qué quiero decir, entonces?
es.R: ¿Qué quiero decir con esto?

sw.L: Basi ninasema nini?
sw.B: Basi ninasema nini hapa?
sw.R: Ninamaanisha nini kwa maneno haya?

vi.L: Vậy tôi đang nói gì?
vi.B: Vậy tôi muốn nói gì?
vi.R: Tôi có ý gì khi nói điều này?

ko.L: 그러면 내가 무엇을 말하는 것입니까?
ko.B: 그러면 내 말은 무슨 뜻입니까?
ko.R: 내가 하는 말은 무슨 뜻입니까?

decisions.choice: Paul heads off a misunderstanding of verses 16-18
decisions.reason: If eating a sacrifice makes one a partner in the altar, someone might think Paul is now saying that idols are real gods. The next question rejects that.

source.text: ὅτι εἰδωλόθυτόν τί ἐστιν, ἢ ὅτι εἴδωλόν τί ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: That [food] offered to an idol anything is, or that an idol anything is?

en.L: That [food] offered to idols is something, or that an idol is something?
en.B: That food offered to idols amounts to anything? Or that an idol is anything at all?
en.R: Am I saying that food offered to idols is special in some way? Or that an idol is a real god?

fr.L: Que [l’aliment] offert aux idoles est quelque chose, ou qu’une idole est quelque chose ?
fr.B: Que les aliments offerts aux idoles ont une quelconque valeur ? Ou qu’une idole est quoi que ce soit ?
fr.R: Est-ce que je dis que la nourriture offerte aux idoles a quelque chose de spécial ? Ou qu’une idole est un vrai dieu ?

es.L: ¿Que [el alimento] ofrecido a los ídolos es algo, o que un ídolo es algo?
es.B: ¿Que los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos tienen alguna importancia? ¿O que un ídolo es algo real?
es.R: ¿Estoy diciendo que los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos tienen algo especial? ¿O que un ídolo es un dios de verdad?

sw.L: Kwamba [chakula] kilichotolewa sadaka kwa sanamu ni kitu, au kwamba sanamu ni kitu?
sw.B: Kwamba chakula kilichotolewa sadaka kwa sanamu kina maana yoyote? Au kwamba sanamu ni kitu chochote?
sw.R: Je, ninasema kwamba chakula kilichotolewa sadaka kwa sanamu ni maalum kwa namna fulani? Au kwamba sanamu ni mungu halisi?

vi.L: Rằng [thức ăn] cúng thần tượng là điều gì đó, hay thần tượng là điều gì đó sao?
vi.B: Rằng thức ăn cúng thần tượng có giá trị gì sao? Hay thần tượng là một cái gì đó sao?
vi.R: Có phải tôi nói rằng thức ăn cúng thần tượng có điều gì đặc biệt không? Hay thần tượng là một vị thần thật không?

ko.L: 우상에게 바쳐진 [음식]이 무엇이라도 된다는 것입니까? 아니면 우상이 무엇이라도 된다는 것입니까?
ko.B: 우상에게 바친 음식이 무슨 의미가 있다는 말입니까? 아니면 우상이 무엇이라도 된다는 말입니까?
ko.R: 우상에게 바친 음식이 무슨 특별한 것이라는 말입니까? 아니면 우상이 진짜 신이라는 말입니까?

decisions.choice: anything: anything real or of importance
decisions.reason: Paul does not take back what he agreed in 8:4: an idol is nothing. The food is just food, and the idol is not a god.

decisions.choice: questions that expect the answer no
decisions.reason: Verse 20 begins with ἀλλ: "no, rather".

decisions.choice: [food] offered to idols (L); food offered to idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: As throughout chapters 8-10 (terms doc).

decisions.choice: [el alimento] ofrecido a los ídolos (L); los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in chapter 8 for this word, so it is never varied.

decisions.choice: [chakula] kilichotolewa sadaka kwa sanamu (L); chakula kilichotolewa sadaka kwa sanamu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The words settled in 8:1 for eidolothyton, never varied, here in the singular.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἃ θύουσιν, δαιμονίοις καὶ οὐ θεῷ θύουσιν, οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς κοινωνοὺς τῶν δαιμονίων γίνεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: But that what they sacrifice, to demons and not to God they sacrifice; not I want but you sharers of the demons to become.

en.L: But that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to become sharers with the demons.
en.B: No. I mean that what people sacrifice to idols, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I do not want you to become partners with demons.
en.R: No. But when people offer sacrifices to idols, they are really offering them to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to join in with demons.

fr.L: Mais que ce qu’ils sacrifient, ils le sacrifient aux démons et non à Dieu ; or je ne veux pas que vous deveniez participants des démons.
fr.B: Non. Je veux dire que ce que les gens sacrifient aux idoles, ils le sacrifient à des démons et non à Dieu. Et je ne veux pas que vous deveniez les associés des démons.
fr.R: Non. Mais quand les gens offrent des sacrifices aux idoles, en réalité, ils les offrent à des démons, pas à Dieu. Et je ne veux pas que vous vous associiez aux démons.

es.L: Sino que lo que sacrifican, a los demonios y no a Dios lo sacrifican; y no quiero que {{plural_you:ustedes se hagan|vosotros os hagáis}} partícipes de los demonios.
es.B: No. Digo que lo que se sacrifica a los ídolos se sacrifica a los demonios y no a Dios. Y no quiero que {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} compañeros de los demonios.
es.R: No. Cuando la gente ofrece sacrificios a los ídolos, en realidad se los ofrece a los demonios, no a Dios. Y no quiero que {{plural_you:se unan|os unáis}} a los demonios.

sw.L: Bali kwamba vitu wanavyovitoa dhabihu, wanavitoa dhabihu kwa pepo wala si kwa Mungu; nami sitaki ninyi mwe washiriki wa pepo.
sw.B: Hapana. Ninamaanisha kwamba vitu ambavyo watu huvitoa dhabihu kwa sanamu, huvitoa kwa pepo wala si kwa Mungu. Nami sitaki ninyi mwe washirika wa pepo.
sw.R: Hapana. Lakini watu wanapotoa dhabihu kwa sanamu, kwa kweli wanazitoa kwa pepo, si kwa Mungu. Nami sitaki ninyi mjiunge na pepo.

vi.L: Nhưng [tôi nói] rằng những gì họ dâng tế, họ dâng tế cho các quỷ chứ không phải cho Đức Chúa Trời; và tôi không muốn anh chị em trở thành những người dự phần với các quỷ.
vi.B: Không. Ý tôi là những gì người ta dâng tế cho thần tượng là dâng tế cho ma quỷ, chứ không phải cho Đức Chúa Trời. Và tôi không muốn anh chị em trở thành những người cùng dự phần với ma quỷ.
vi.R: Không. Nhưng khi người ta dâng sinh tế cho thần tượng, thật ra họ đang dâng cho ma quỷ, chứ không phải cho Đức Chúa Trời. Và tôi không muốn anh chị em nhập bọn với ma quỷ.

ko.L: 아닙니다. 그들이 제물로 바치는 것은 귀신들에게 바치는 것이지 하나님께 바치는 것이 아니라는 것입니다. 나는 여러분이 귀신들과 함께 참여하는 사람이 되기를 원하지 않습니다.
ko.B: 아닙니다. 사람들이 우상에게 바치는 제물은 하나님께 바치는 것이 아니라 귀신들에게 바치는 것이라는 뜻입니다. 나는 여러분이 귀신들과 한편이 되기를 원하지 않습니다.
ko.R: 그렇지 않습니다. 사람들이 우상에게 제물을 바칠 때, 그들은 사실 하나님이 아니라 귀신들에게 바치는 것입니다. 나는 여러분이 귀신들과 어울리기를 원하지 않습니다.

decisions.choice: they sacrifice to demons and not to God: the words of Deuteronomy 32:17
decisions.reason: In the Song of Moses Israel "sacrificed to demons and not to God" (Deuteronomy 32:17 in the Greek Old Testament). The phrase can also be read "to what is not God". Paul uses the words of Scripture for pagan worship in Corinth. Verse 22 echoes the same song.

decisions.choice: demons: evil spiritual beings opposed to God
alternatives: the gods of the pagans, thought of as real
decisions.reason: The idol is nothing (verse 19), but the worship given to it is not neutral: spiritual powers opposed to God stand behind it. δαιμονίοις is the usual word for evil spirits in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "what they sacrifice", with no stated subject
alternatives: "what the Gentiles sacrifice", with the words "the Gentiles" added, found in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add a subject, "the Gentiles"; others, including early ones, lack it. The meaning is the same either way: the sacrifices of pagan worship. The SBLGNT text governs. The evidence here is described from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: partners: people who share in something with others
decisions.reason: κοινωνοὺς is the word of verse 18 ("sharers in the altar"). Eating at a sacrificial meal joins a person to the one worshiped there.

decisions.choice: people ... to idols
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the subject unstated (m3); Balanced and Readable say who is meant.

decisions.choice: partners (B); join in with (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sharers", as in verse 18; Balanced uses a word that suits people sharing a meal and a loyalty.

decisions.choice: partícipes (L); compañeros (B); unirse a (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a partner who shares in something with others (m4). Literal says "partícipes", as in verse 18; Balanced "compañeros" and Readable "unirse a", as the English says "partners" and "join in with".

decisions.choice: pepo
decisions.reason: "Pepo" for daimonia, as in the Gospels; "roho" is kept for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit, and "Shetani" for Satan alone.

decisions.choice: "các quỷ" (L); "ma quỷ" (B, R) for daimonia (also 10:21)
decisions.reason: "Quỷ" is the word of the Vietnamese Gospels for demons (Mark 1:34). "Ma quỷ" is the everyday word for evil spirits; here it is plural in sense, not the devil.

decisions.choice: "귀신" for demons at every level
decisions.reason: "귀신" is the word of the Gospels for demons (Mark 16:17); "마귀" is kept for the devil.

source.text: οὐ δύνασθε ποτήριον κυρίου πίνειν καὶ ποτήριον δαιμονίων· οὐ δύνασθε τραπέζης κυρίου μετέχειν καὶ τραπέζης δαιμονίων.

records.literal_gloss: Not you are able cup of Lord to drink and cup of demons; not you are able of table of Lord to partake and of table of demons.

en.L: You are not able to drink a cup of [the] Lord and a cup of demons; you are not able to share in a table of [the] Lord and a table of demons.
en.B: It is impossible for you to drink from the Lord's cup and from a cup of demons as well, or to eat at the Lord's table and at a demons' table.
en.R: You cannot drink from the Lord's cup and also from the cup used to honor demons. You cannot eat at the Lord's table and also at a table where demons are honored.

fr.L: Vous ne pouvez pas boire une coupe du Seigneur et une coupe de démons ; vous ne pouvez pas avoir part à une table du Seigneur et à une table de démons.
fr.B: Il vous est impossible de boire à la coupe du Seigneur et aussi à une coupe des démons, ou de manger à la table du Seigneur et à une table des démons.
fr.R: Vous ne pouvez pas boire à la coupe du Seigneur et aussi à la coupe qui sert à honorer des démons. Vous ne pouvez pas manger à la table du Seigneur et aussi à une table où l’on honore des démons.

es.L: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} beber [la] copa del Señor y [la] copa de demonios; no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} participar de [la] mesa del Señor y de [la] mesa de demonios.
es.B: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} beber de la copa del Señor y también de una copa de demonios, ni comer en la mesa del Señor y también en una mesa de demonios.
es.R: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} beber de la copa del Señor y también de la copa que se usa para honrar a los demonios. No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} comer en la mesa del Señor y también en una mesa donde se honra a los demonios.

sw.L: Hamwezi kunywa kikombe cha Bwana na kikombe cha pepo; hamwezi kushiriki meza ya Bwana na meza ya pepo.
sw.B: Haiwezekani ninyi kunywa kutoka kikombe cha Bwana na pia kutoka kikombe cha pepo, au kula mezani pa Bwana na pia mezani pa pepo.
sw.R: Hamwezi kunywa kutoka kikombe cha Bwana na pia kutoka kikombe kinachotumiwa kuwaheshimu pepo. Hamwezi kula mezani pa Bwana na pia mezani ambapo pepo wanaheshimiwa.

vi.L: Anh chị em không thể uống chén của Chúa và chén của các quỷ; anh chị em không thể dự phần bàn của Chúa và bàn của các quỷ.
vi.B: Anh chị em không thể vừa uống chén của Chúa vừa uống chén của ma quỷ, hay vừa ăn ở bàn của Chúa vừa ăn ở bàn của ma quỷ.
vi.R: Anh chị em không thể uống chén của Chúa mà cũng uống chén dùng để tôn vinh ma quỷ. Anh chị em không thể ăn ở bàn của Chúa mà cũng ăn ở bàn nơi ma quỷ được tôn vinh.

ko.L: 여러분은 주님의 잔과 귀신들의 잔을 마실 수 없습니다. 여러분은 주님의 식탁과 귀신들의 식탁에 참여할 수 없습니다.
ko.B: 여러분이 주님의 잔을 마시면서 귀신들의 잔도 마실 수는 없습니다. 주님의 식탁에서 먹으면서 귀신들의 식탁에서도 먹을 수는 없습니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 주님의 잔을 마시면서, 귀신들을 높이는 데 쓰는 잔도 마실 수는 없습니다. 주님의 식탁에서 먹으면서, 귀신들을 높이는 식탁에서도 먹을 수는 없습니다.

decisions.choice: the table of demons: meals in honor of a pagan god in its temple
decisions.reason: Papyrus invitations survive in which a person is invited "to dine at the table of the lord Sarapis". Pagan meals were held in the god's name, with the god thought of as host. The table of the Lord is the Lord's Supper, where Christ is the host.

decisions.choice: the table of the Lord: the altar of the Lord in Malachi
decisions.reason: Malachi 1:7, 12 calls the altar "the table of the LORD"; there the Hebrew has the divine name. Here "Lord" is the Lord Jesus, whose cup and bread are shared in verse 16.

decisions.choice: cannot: the two are incompatible, not physically impossible
decisions.reason: Some Corinthians did both. Paul means that a person cannot belong to both at once: loyalty to the Lord excludes taking part in the worship of other powers.

decisions.choice: It is impossible for you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the force of "you are not able" (m3) and joins the two halves into one sentence.

decisions.choice: the cup used to honor demons; a table where demons are honored
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase "of demons" (m1).

decisions.choice: "주님의 식탁" (L, B, R), "주님의 잔"
decisions.reason: "식탁" is the plain current word for a table at a meal; the meaning decision reads "Lord" as the Lord Jesus, with the honorific "주님".

source.text: ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον;

records.literal_gloss: Or do we provoke to jealousy the Lord?

en.L: Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy?
en.B: Or do we mean to stir up the Lord's jealousy?
en.R: Do we really want to make the Lord jealous?

fr.L: Ou bien provoquons-nous la jalousie du Seigneur ?
fr.B: Voulons-nous donc éveiller la jalousie du Seigneur ?
fr.R: Voulons-nous vraiment rendre le Seigneur jaloux ?

es.L: ¿O provocamos a celos al Señor?
es.B: ¿O es que queremos despertar los celos del Señor?
es.R: ¿De verdad queremos poner celoso al Señor?

sw.L: Au je, tunamtia Bwana wivu?
sw.B: Au tunataka kuuchochea wivu wa Bwana?
sw.R: Je, kweli tunataka kumfanya Bwana aone wivu?

vi.L: Hay chúng ta đang khiến Chúa ghen?
vi.B: Hay chúng ta muốn khơi dậy lòng ghen của Chúa?
vi.R: Chúng ta có thật muốn làm cho Chúa ghen không?

ko.L: 아니면 우리가 주님을 질투하시게 하려는 것입니까?
ko.B: 아니면 우리가 주님의 질투를 일으키려는 것입니까?
ko.R: 우리가 정말 주님께서 질투하시게 만들고 싶습니까?

decisions.choice: provoke to jealousy: Deuteronomy 32:21, where Israel provoked God to jealousy with idols
decisions.reason: In the Song of Moses God says that Israel made him jealous with what is no god (Deuteronomy 32:16, 21). Paul has just used the same song in verse 20. There the one provoked is the LORD; the Hebrew has the divine name.

decisions.choice: the Lord's jealousy: his rightful claim to his people's whole loyalty, as a husband's claim on his wife
decisions.reason: God's jealousy is not petty envy but the love that will not share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14). Here "the Lord" is Christ, the Lord of the table (verse 21), to whom Paul gives what Scripture says of God.

decisions.choice: or: an alternative put as a warning question
decisions.reason: If they try to eat at both tables, are they daring the Lord to act, as Israel did?

decisions.choice: stir up the Lord's jealousy
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plainer verb; "do we mean to" brings out the warning in the question.

decisions.choice: "ghen" for the Lord's jealousy
decisions.reason: In the Vietnamese Romans 10:19, "ganh tị" is Israel's jealousy of the nations; the Lord's jealousy is the rightful claim of a husband on his wife (m2), which Vietnamese calls "ghen".

decisions.choice: "질투하시다", "질투" at every level
decisions.reason: Romans 10:19 uses "시기하게 하다" for God making Israel envious of others; here it is the Lord's own jealousy over his people, as in Deuteronomy 32:21, which Korean calls "질투".

source.text: μὴ ἰσχυρότεροι αὐτοῦ ἐσμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Not stronger than him are we?

en.L: We are not stronger than {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, are we?
en.B: Do we think we are stronger than {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is?
en.R: Do we think we are stronger than the Lord?

fr.L: Nous ne sommes pas plus forts que {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.B: Pensons-nous être plus forts que {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ?
fr.R: Pensons-nous être plus forts que le Seigneur ?

es.L: ¿Acaso somos más fuertes que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?
es.B: ¿Creemos que somos más fuertes que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?
es.R: ¿Creemos que somos más fuertes que el Señor?

sw.L: Hatuna nguvu kuliko {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, sivyo?
sw.B: Je, tunadhani tuna nguvu kuliko {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}?
sw.R: Je, tunadhani tuna nguvu kuliko Bwana?

vi.L: Chúng ta đâu có mạnh hơn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, phải không?
vi.B: Chúng ta tưởng mình mạnh hơn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sao?
vi.R: Chúng ta nghĩ mình mạnh hơn Chúa sao?

ko.L: 우리가 그분보다 강하다는 말입니까?
ko.B: 우리가 그분보다 더 강하다고 생각합니까?
ko.R: 우리가 주님보다 더 강하다고 생각합니까?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: μὴ shows that the answer must be no: no one can defy the Lord and escape his judgment.

decisions.choice: stronger: perhaps a jab at those who thought of themselves as strong
decisions.reason: In 4:10 Paul says with irony, "you are strong". Those who felt free to eat in idol temples may have counted themselves the strong, as opposed to the weak of chapter 8. Paul asks whether they are stronger than the Lord.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: A pronoun for the Lord. Readable names him.

source.text: Πάντα ἔξεστιν· ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει.

records.literal_gloss: All things are lawful; but not all things are beneficial.

en.L: "All things are permitted"; but not all things are of benefit.
en.B: "Everything is permitted." Yes, but not everything is for the good.
en.R: Some of you say, "Everything is allowed." That may be true, but not everything is good for you.

fr.L: « Tout est permis » ; mais tout n’est pas utile.
fr.B: « Tout est permis. » Oui, mais tout ne fait pas du bien.
fr.R: Certains d’entre vous disent : « Tout est permis. » C’est peut-être vrai, mais tout n’est pas bon pour vous.

es.L: «Todo está permitido»; pero no todo conviene.
es.B: «Todo está permitido». Sí, pero no todo es para bien.
es.R: Algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} dicen: «Se permite hacer cualquier cosa». Puede que sea así, pero no todo {{plural_you:les|os}} hace bien.

sw.L: "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa"; lakini si kila kitu kinafaa.
sw.B: "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa." Ndiyo, lakini si kila kitu kinaleta mema.
sw.R: Baadhi yenu mnasema, "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa." Huenda ni kweli, lakini si kila kitu ni chema kwenu.

vi.L: "Mọi sự đều được phép"; nhưng không phải mọi sự đều có ích.
vi.B: "Mọi điều đều được phép." Đúng vậy, nhưng không phải mọi điều đều đem lại điều tốt.
vi.R: Có người trong anh chị em nói: "Điều gì cũng được phép." Có thể là như vậy, nhưng không phải điều gì cũng tốt cho anh chị em.

ko.L: "모든 것이 허용되어 있다." 그러나 모든 것이 유익한 것은 아닙니다.
ko.B: "모든 것이 허용되어 있다." 그렇습니다. 그러나 모든 것이 유익한 것은 아닙니다.
ko.R: 여러분 가운데 어떤 사람은 "무엇이든지 해도 된다" 하고 말합니다. 그 말이 맞을지도 모릅니다. 그러나 모든 것이 여러분에게 좋은 것은 아닙니다.

decisions.choice: the Corinthian saying of 6:12, quoted again and marked as a quotation
alternatives: Paul's own principle, which he then limits
decisions.reason: As in 6:12 (12.s1, m1): the Greek has no quotation marks, but the same saying returns, again answered by Paul's "but". Here the saying lacks "to me", and Paul's answer measures freedom by the good of others (verse 24).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "to me" in the saying
alternatives: "all things are permitted to me", found in later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts add "to me" here, probably to match 6:12. The SBLGNT text governs. The evidence here is described from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: beneficial: doing real good, here above all to others
decisions.reason: As in 6:12. Verse 24 and verse 33 show that the good Paul has in mind is the good of others.

decisions.choice: permitted (L, B); allowed (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as 6:12, so the reader hears the saying return.

decisions.choice: Yes, but (B); Some of you say ... That may be true, but (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:12 (r-en-2 there).

decisions.choice: «Todo está permitido» (L, B); Algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} dicen: «...» (R)
decisions.reason: The Corinthian saying of 6:12 comes back in «» marks with the same words, without "me", which the Greek here does not have (m2).

decisions.choice: "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa"
decisions.reason: The saying of 6:12 again, in the same words, but without "kwangu" (to me), which the text followed here lacks (meaning decision); "Baadhi yenu mnasema" in Readable as in 6:12.

decisions.choice: the Corinthian saying of 6:12 in the same words and quotation marks
decisions.reason: The same saying returns, so Korean keeps the words of 6:12.

source.text: πάντα ἔξεστιν· ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα οἰκοδομεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: All things are lawful; but not all things build up.

en.L: "All things are permitted"; but not all things build up.
en.B: "Everything is permitted." Yes, but not everything builds others up.
en.R: "Everything is allowed." Yes, but not everything makes others strong.

fr.L: « Tout est permis » ; mais tout n’édifie pas.
fr.B: « Tout est permis. » Oui, mais tout n’édifie pas les autres.
fr.R: « Tout est permis. » Oui, mais tout ne rend pas les autres plus forts.

es.L: «Todo está permitido»; pero no todo edifica.
es.B: «Todo está permitido». Sí, pero no todo edifica a los demás.
es.R: «Se permite hacer cualquier cosa». Sí, pero no todo fortalece a los demás.

sw.L: "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa"; lakini si kila kitu hujenga.
sw.B: "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa." Ndiyo, lakini si kila kitu huwajenga wengine.
sw.R: "Kila kitu kimeruhusiwa." Ndiyo, lakini si kila kitu huwaimarisha wengine.

vi.L: "Mọi sự đều được phép"; nhưng không phải mọi sự đều gây dựng.
vi.B: "Mọi điều đều được phép." Đúng vậy, nhưng không phải mọi điều đều gây dựng người khác.
vi.R: "Điều gì cũng được phép." Đúng vậy, nhưng không phải điều gì cũng làm cho người khác vững mạnh.

ko.L: "모든 것이 허용되어 있다." 그러나 모든 것이 세워 주는 것은 아닙니다.
ko.B: "모든 것이 허용되어 있다." 그렇습니다. 그러나 모든 것이 다른 사람을 세워 주는 것은 아닙니다.
ko.R: "무엇이든지 해도 된다." 그렇습니다. 그러나 모든 것이 다른 사람을 굳세게 해 주는 것은 아닙니다.

decisions.choice: the Corinthian saying again, marked as a quotation
decisions.reason: As in the first half of the verse (23.s1, m1).

decisions.choice: build up: strengthen others and the church
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομεῖ is the verb of 8:1: "knowledge puffs up, but love builds up". The test of freedom is whether it helps others grow.

decisions.choice: others
alternatives: no object, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: As in 8:1, Balanced and Readable supply the object to show who is built up.

decisions.choice: makes others strong
decisions.reason: As in 8:1 (Readable).

decisions.choice: edifica (L, B); fortalece (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:1: "edificar" for building up others at Literal and Balanced, "fortalecer" at Readable.

decisions.choice: hujenga (L); huwajenga wengine (B); huwaimarisha wengine (R)
decisions.reason: The verb "kujenga" as in 8:1 (love builds up), and "kuimarisha" in Readable as there.

source.text: μηδεὶς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ζητείτω ἀλλὰ τὸ τοῦ ἑτέρου.

records.literal_gloss: No one the of himself let seek but that of the other.

en.L: Let no one seek what is {{gender:their|his}} own, but what is the other's.
en.B: No one should look for {{gender:their|his}} own advantage, but for the other person's.
en.R: Do not think only about what is good for you. Think about what is good for other people.

fr.L: Que personne ne cherche son propre [intérêt], mais celui de l’autre.
fr.B: Que personne ne recherche son propre avantage, mais celui de l’autre.
fr.R: Ne pensez pas seulement à ce qui est bon pour vous. Pensez à ce qui est bon pour les autres.

es.L: Que nadie busque lo suyo propio, sino lo del otro.
es.B: Nadie debe buscar su propio provecho, sino el del otro.
es.R: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} solo en lo que es bueno para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en lo que es bueno para los demás.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote asitafute [faida] yake mwenyewe, bali ya mwingine.
sw.B: Mtu asitafute faida yake mwenyewe, bali faida ya mtu mwingine.
sw.R: Msifikirie tu kile kilicho chema kwenu. Fikirieni kile kilicho chema kwa watu wengine.

vi.L: Đừng ai tìm lợi ích cho chính mình, nhưng [tìm lợi ích] cho người khác.
vi.B: Đừng ai tìm lợi ích riêng cho mình, nhưng hãy tìm lợi ích cho người khác.
vi.R: Đừng chỉ nghĩ đến điều tốt cho mình. Hãy nghĩ đến điều tốt cho người khác.

ko.L: 아무도 자기 것을 구하지 말고 다른 사람의 것을 구하십시오.
ko.B: 아무도 자기 유익을 구하지 말고 다른 사람의 유익을 구하십시오.
ko.R: 자기에게 좋은 것만 생각하지 마십시오. 다른 사람들에게 좋은 것을 생각하십시오.

decisions.choice: not one's own but the other's: put the good of others first
alternatives: never think of oneself at all
decisions.reason: The sharp "not ... but" sets priorities, as in Philippians 2:4. Verse 33 says the same of Paul: he seeks the good of many.

decisions.choice: the other: the other person, especially the fellow believer whose conscience is weak
decisions.reason: ἑτέρου is "the other one", whoever is affected. In this passage that includes the weak believer (8:9-13) and the unbeliever at a meal (verses 27-29).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The command is for everyone, man or woman.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the contrast is about what comes first (m1).

decisions.choice: "personne ... son", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:their|his}}. French "personne" already means no one at all, man or woman, and "son" agrees with the thing possessed, so the sentence is inclusive as it stands (style guide 7).

decisions.choice: lo suyo, su, no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "suyo" and "su" mean his or her, so the English setting ({{gender:their|his}}) has nothing to change, as in 3:8.

source.text: πᾶν τὸ ἐν μακέλλῳ πωλούμενον ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν, τοῦ κυρίου γὰρ ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Everything that in meat market being sold eat, nothing examining on account of the conscience; \v 26 of the Lord for the earth and the fullness of it.

en.L: Everything being sold in [the] meat market, eat, examining nothing for the sake of conscience; \v 26 for "the Lord's [is] the earth, and its fullness."
en.B: You may eat whatever is on sale in the meat market without asking questions for conscience' sake, \v 26 because "the earth belongs to the Lord, and everything that fills it."
en.R: When you buy meat at the market, you can eat any of it. You do not need to ask where it came from to keep your conscience clear. \v 26 The Scriptures say, "The earth and everything in it belong to the Lord."

fr.L: Tout ce qui se vend au marché de la viande, mangez-le, sans rien examiner à cause de la conscience ; \v 26 car « au Seigneur [est] la terre, et ce qui la remplit ».
fr.B: Vous pouvez manger tout ce qui se vend au marché de la viande sans poser de questions par scrupule de conscience, \v 26 car « la terre appartient au Seigneur, avec tout ce qui la remplit ».
fr.R: Quand vous achetez de la viande au marché, vous pouvez en manger. Vous n’avez pas besoin de demander d’où elle vient pour avoir la conscience tranquille. \v 26 Les Écritures disent : « La terre et tout ce qu’elle contient appartiennent au Seigneur. »

es.L: Todo lo que se vende en el mercado de carne, {{plural_you:cómanlo|comedlo}}, sin examinar nada por causa de la conciencia; \v 26 porque «del Señor [es] la tierra y su plenitud».
es.B: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} comer de todo lo que se vende en el mercado de carne, sin hacer preguntas por motivos de conciencia, \v 26 porque «la tierra es del Señor, y todo lo que la llena».
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:compren|compréis}} carne en el mercado, {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} comer cualquiera. No {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} preguntar de dónde viene para tener la conciencia tranquila. \v 26 Las Escrituras dicen: «La tierra y todo lo que hay en ella pertenecen al Señor».

sw.L: Kila kinachouzwa katika soko la nyama, kuleni, bila kuuliza chochote kwa ajili ya dhamiri; \v 26 kwa maana "dunia [ni] ya Bwana, na vyote vilivyomo ndani yake."
sw.B: Mnaweza kula chochote kinachouzwa katika soko la nyama bila kuuliza maswali kwa ajili ya dhamiri, \v 26 kwa sababu "dunia ni mali ya Bwana, pamoja na vyote vilivyomo."
sw.R: Mnaponunua nyama sokoni, mnaweza kula nyama yoyote. Hamna haja ya kuuliza ilikotoka ili dhamiri yenu ibaki safi. \v 26 Maandiko yanasema, "Dunia na kila kitu kilichomo ni mali ya Bwana."

vi.L: Mọi thứ được bán ở chợ thịt, hãy ăn, không tra xét gì vì cớ lương tâm; \v 26 vì "đất và mọi vật đầy dẫy trên đất đều thuộc về Chúa."
vi.B: Anh chị em có thể ăn bất cứ thứ gì bán ở chợ thịt mà không cần hỏi han gì vì cớ lương tâm, \v 26 bởi vì "đất và mọi vật đầy dẫy trên đất đều thuộc về Chúa."
vi.R: Khi mua thịt ở chợ, anh chị em có thể ăn bất cứ thứ thịt nào. Anh chị em không cần hỏi thịt ấy từ đâu ra để giữ cho lương tâm mình yên ổn. \v 26 Kinh Thánh chép: "Đất và mọi vật trên đất đều thuộc về Chúa."

ko.L: 시장에서 팔리는 것은 무엇이든지 양심을 위하여 아무것도 묻지 말고 먹으십시오. \v 26 "땅과 그 안에 가득한 것이 주의 것"이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 시장에서 파는 고기는 무엇이든지 양심 때문에 묻고 따지지 말고 먹어도 됩니다. \v 26 "땅과 그 안에 있는 모든 것이 주님의 것"이기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 시장에서 고기를 사면 어떤 고기든지 먹어도 됩니다. 양심을 깨끗하게 지키려고 그 고기가 어디서 왔는지 물어볼 필요가 없습니다. \v 26 성경에 "땅과 그 안에 있는 모든 것이 주님의 것이다" 하고 쓰여 있습니다.

decisions.choice: the meat market: the city's market where meat and other food were sold
decisions.reason: μακέλλῳ is a market building for meat, fish and other food. Corinth had one, known from inscriptions. Some of the meat sold there came from temple sacrifices, and buyers could not always tell which.

decisions.choice: examining: asking questions about where the meat came from
decisions.reason: ἀνακρίνοντες is the verb of 2:14-15 and 4:3-4, to examine or inquire into. Paul tells them not to investigate the meat's history.

decisions.choice: for the sake of conscience: so that conscience will not be troubled
decisions.reason: There is no need to ask, since the food itself is clean (verse 26). Asking would only raise scruples where there need be none. Verses 28-29 show when conscience does come into it.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 24:1 (23:1 in the Greek Old Testament)
decisions.reason: The words match the Greek of the psalm. Where the Greek has κυρίου, the Hebrew has the divine name, YHWH. Later Jewish teaching used this verse to show that one should give thanks before eating, since all food belongs to God.

decisions.choice: eat: the imperative grants permission
alternatives: a command that everyone must eat
decisions.reason: Paul is not ordering them to eat but freeing them to eat whatever is sold.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the psalm with the Greek word for "Lord", so the text says "Lord", as in John 1:23 and 1 Corinthians 1:31; m4 notes the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: You may eat ... without asking questions (B); you can eat ... You do not need to ask (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the imperative grants permission (m5); "examine" (Literal) is kept for the courtroom sense in chapters 2 and 4.

decisions.choice: The Scriptures say
decisions.reason: Readable says that these words are a quotation.

decisions.choice: examinar
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "examinar", the word used for this verb since 2:14; Balanced and Readable say "hacer preguntas", the sense here (m2).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} comer
decisions.reason: The command grants permission (m5), so Balanced and Readable say "pueden comer", as the English says "you may eat".

decisions.choice: "Chúa", not "CHÚA", in this quotation of Psalm 24:1
decisions.reason: As in 2:16 and 3:20: the Greek has kyrios; the Hebrew of the psalm has the divine name (m4).

decisions.choice: "주" (L); "주님" (B, R) in the psalm, with no divine_name span
decisions.reason: The psalm has the divine name; Paul's Greek has "Lord", given as in Romans' quotations.

decisions.choice: "묻다" (L); "묻고 따지다" (B) for the verb of 2:14-15 here
decisions.reason: The verb that Literal elsewhere gives as "살피다" here means asking questions about where the meat came from, so Korean says "묻다".

source.text: εἴ τις καλεῖ ὑμᾶς τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ θέλετε πορεύεσθαι, πᾶν τὸ παρατιθέμενον ὑμῖν ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν·

records.literal_gloss: If anyone invites you of the unbelievers and you want to go, everything being set before you eat, nothing examining on account of the conscience;

en.L: If any of the unbelievers invites you and you want to go, eat everything set before you, examining nothing for the sake of conscience.
en.B: Suppose an unbeliever asks you to dinner and you decide to go. Then eat whatever is served, and do not ask questions for conscience' sake.
en.R: Someone who does not believe in Jesus may invite you to a meal at their home. If you want to go, eat whatever food they give you. You do not need to ask where it came from to keep your conscience clear.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un des incroyants vous invite et que vous voulez y aller, mangez tout ce qui vous est servi, sans rien examiner à cause de la conscience.
fr.B: Supposez qu’un incroyant vous invite à dîner et que vous décidiez d’y aller. Alors mangez tout ce qu’on vous sert, sans poser de questions par scrupule de conscience.
fr.R: Quelqu’un qui ne croit pas en Jésus vous invitera peut-être à un repas chez lui. Si vous voulez y aller, mangez tout ce qu’on vous donne. Vous n’avez pas besoin de demander d’où vient la nourriture pour avoir la conscience tranquille.

es.L: Si alguno de los no creyentes {{plural_you:los|os}} invita y {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} ir, {{plural_you:coman|comed}} de todo lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} ponga delante, sin examinar nada por causa de la conciencia.
es.B: Si un no creyente {{plural_you:los|os}} invita a comer y {{plural_you:deciden|decidís}} ir, {{plural_you:coman|comed}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} sirvan, sin hacer preguntas por motivos de conciencia.
es.R: Puede que alguien que no cree en Jesús {{plural_you:los|os}} invite a comer a su casa. Si {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} ir, {{plural_you:coman|comed}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} den. No {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} preguntar de dónde viene para tener la conciencia tranquila.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote miongoni mwa wasioamini akiwaalika, nanyi mkitaka kwenda, kuleni kila kitu kinachowekwa mbele yenu, bila kuuliza chochote kwa ajili ya dhamiri.
sw.B: Tuseme mtu asiyeamini anawaalika chakulani, nanyi mmeamua kwenda. Basi kuleni chochote mnachopakuliwa, wala msiulize maswali kwa ajili ya dhamiri.
sw.R: Huenda mtu asiyemwamini Yesu akawaalika kula chakula nyumbani kwake. Mkitaka kwenda, kuleni chakula chochote atakachowapa. Hamna haja ya kuuliza kilikotoka ili dhamiri yenu ibaki safi.

vi.L: Nếu có người nào trong những người không tin mời anh chị em và anh chị em muốn đi, thì hãy ăn mọi thứ được dọn ra cho anh chị em, không tra xét gì vì cớ lương tâm.
vi.B: Giả sử một người không tin Chúa mời anh chị em dùng bữa và anh chị em quyết định đi. Thì hãy ăn bất cứ món gì được dọn ra, đừng hỏi han gì vì cớ lương tâm.
vi.R: Một người không tin Đức Giê-xu có thể mời anh chị em đến nhà họ dùng bữa. Nếu anh chị em muốn đi, hãy ăn bất cứ món gì họ dọn ra. Anh chị em không cần hỏi món ăn ấy từ đâu ra để giữ cho lương tâm mình yên ổn.

ko.L: 믿지 않는 사람들 가운데 누가 여러분을 초대하여 여러분이 가고 싶으면, 여러분 앞에 차려 놓은 것은 무엇이든지 양심을 위하여 아무것도 묻지 말고 먹으십시오.
ko.B: 믿지 않는 사람이 여러분을 식사에 초대하여 여러분이 가기로 했다면, 차려 주는 것은 무엇이든지 양심 때문에 묻고 따지지 말고 먹으십시오.
ko.R: 예수님을 믿지 않는 사람이 여러분을 자기 집 식사에 초대할 수도 있습니다. 여러분이 가고 싶으면, 그 사람이 내놓는 음식은 무엇이든지 먹으십시오. 양심을 깨끗하게 지키려고 그 음식이 어디서 왔는지 물어볼 필요가 없습니다.

decisions.choice: a meal in a private home, not in a temple
alternatives: a meal in a temple dining room
decisions.reason: Verses 14-22 have ruled out meals at an idol's table. Here the setting is a meal served by an unbelieving host, where the food might or might not come from a sacrifice.

decisions.choice: unbelievers: people outside the church
decisions.reason: ἀπίστων is used throughout this letter for those who do not believe (6:6; 7:12-15; 14:22-24).

decisions.choice: and you want to go: Paul neither commands nor forbids accepting
decisions.reason: Accepting such an invitation is left to the believer.

decisions.choice: examining nothing for the sake of conscience: as in verse 25
decisions.reason: See 25.s1, m2 and m3.

decisions.choice: does not believe in Jesus; at their home
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the unbelievers are and makes the setting explicit (m1).

decisions.choice: asks you to dinner
decisions.reason: The invitation is to a meal, as the rest of the verse shows.

source.text: ἐὰν δέ τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τοῦτο ἱερόθυτόν ἐστιν, μὴ ἐσθίετε δι’ ἐκεῖνον τὸν μηνύσαντα καὶ τὴν συνείδησιν·

records.literal_gloss: If but anyone to you says: This sacrificed-to-a-god is, not eat on account of that [one] having informed and the conscience;

en.L: But if anyone says to you, "This is [meat] offered in sacrifice," do not eat [it], because of that one who informed [you] and because of conscience.
en.B: But if anyone points out to you, "This came from a temple sacrifice," leave it uneaten. Do so out of regard for the person who pointed it out, and because of conscience.
en.R: But someone may say to you, "This meat was offered to a god." Then do not eat it. Do this for the sake of the person who told you, and because of that person's conscience.

fr.L: Mais si quelqu’un vous dit : « Ceci est [une viande] offerte en sacrifice », n’[en] mangez pas, à cause de celui qui [vous] a avertis et à cause de la conscience.
fr.B: Mais si quelqu’un vous fait remarquer : « Ceci provient d’un sacrifice au temple », abstenez-vous d’en manger. Faites-le par égard pour celui qui vous l’a signalé, et à cause de la conscience.
fr.R: Mais quelqu’un vous dira peut-être : « Cette viande a été offerte à un dieu. » Alors n’en mangez pas. Faites-le pour celui qui vous l’a dit, et à cause de sa conscience.

es.L: Pero si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} dice: «Esto es [carne] ofrecida en sacrificio», no [la] {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}, por causa de aquel que [{{plural_you:les|os}}] avisó y por causa de la conciencia.
es.B: Pero si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} advierte: «Esto viene de un sacrificio del templo», no lo {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} por consideración a quien {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} advirtió, y por motivos de conciencia.
es.R: Pero puede que alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} diga: «Esta carne fue ofrecida a un dios». Entonces no la {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} por esa persona que {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} dijo, y por la conciencia de esa persona.

sw.L: Lakini mtu yeyote akiwaambia, "Hii ni [nyama] iliyotolewa dhabihu," msiile, kwa ajili ya yule aliyewaarifu, na kwa ajili ya dhamiri.
sw.B: Lakini mtu akiwaonyesha, "Hii imetoka kwenye dhabihu ya hekaluni," msiile. Fanyeni hivyo kwa kumjali yule aliyewaambia, na kwa ajili ya dhamiri.
sw.R: Lakini mtu anaweza kuwaambia, "Nyama hii ilitolewa sadaka kwa mungu." Basi msiile. Fanyeni hivyo kwa ajili ya mtu huyo aliyewaambia, na kwa ajili ya dhamiri yake.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu có ai nói với anh chị em: "Đây là [thịt] đã dâng tế," thì đừng ăn, vì cớ người đã báo cho biết và vì cớ lương tâm.
vi.B: Nhưng nếu có ai lưu ý anh chị em: "Món này là của tế lễ trong đền thần," thì đừng ăn. Hãy làm như vậy vì quý trọng người đã cho biết, và vì cớ lương tâm.
vi.R: Nhưng có thể có người nói với anh chị em: "Thịt này đã được dâng cho thần." Vậy thì đừng ăn. Hãy làm như vậy vì người đã cho anh chị em biết, và vì lương tâm của người ấy.

ko.L: 그러나 누가 여러분에게 "이것은 제사에 바쳐진 [고기]입니다" 하고 말하면, 그렇게 알려 준 사람을 위하여, 그리고 양심을 위하여 먹지 마십시오.
ko.B: 그러나 누가 여러분에게 "이것은 신전 제사에 쓴 고기입니다" 하고 알려 주면, 먹지 말고 그대로 두십시오. 그렇게 알려 준 사람을 생각하고, 또 양심을 생각해서 그렇게 하십시오.
ko.R: 그러나 누가 여러분에게 "이 고기는 신에게 바친 것입니다" 하고 말할 수도 있습니다. 그러면 그것을 먹지 마십시오. 그렇게 말해 준 사람을 위해서, 그리고 그 사람의 양심을 위해서 그렇게 하십시오.

decisions.choice: offered in sacrifice: the polite word for sacrificial meat, used by a non-Jew
decisions.reason: ἱερόθυτόν means "offered in a sacred rite". Elsewhere Paul uses εἰδωλόθυτον, "offered to idols", the word Jews and Christians used (8:1, m2). The polite word suggests that the speaker is not a believer, or is speaking in a pagan setting.

decisions.choice: the one who informed you: probably a fellow guest or the host, perhaps a believer with a weak conscience
decisions.reason: Paul does not say who it is. The polite word fits an unbeliever who assumes that a Christian would care; a weak believer is also possible. Either way, eating after being told would seem to approve of idol worship in that person's eyes.

decisions.choice: because of conscience: the other person's conscience, as verse 29 explains
decisions.reason: The believer's own conscience is not at stake; the informer's is (verse 29).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the verse ends with "and conscience"
alternatives: the words of Psalm 24:1 repeated at the end, "for the earth is the Lord's and its fullness", found in later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts repeat the quotation of verse 26 here. It is missing from the early manuscripts and adds nothing to the sense. The SBLGNT text governs. The evidence here is described from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: [meat] offered in sacrifice (L); came from a temple sacrifice (B); offered to a god (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase "food offered to idols" is kept for the Christian word (terms doc). Here the speaker uses a different, neutral word, so a different phrase is used.

decisions.choice: that person's conscience
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit whose conscience is meant, as verse 29 says (m3).

decisions.choice: leave it uneaten
decisions.reason: The sense is the same; the wording marks the change from verse 27.

decisions.choice: [carne] ofrecida en sacrificio (L); viene de un sacrificio del templo (B); fue ofrecida a un dios (R)
decisions.reason: This is a different, polite word from the one used for food offered to idols (m1), so Spanish does not use "ofrecido a los ídolos" here, and each level follows the English.

decisions.choice: [nyama] iliyotolewa dhabihu (L); imetoka kwenye dhabihu ya hekaluni (B); ilitolewa sadaka kwa mungu (R)
decisions.reason: A different Greek word from eidolothyton, the polite term a non-Jew would use, so it is not given the settled words for "food offered to idols"; lowercase "mungu" for the pagan god.

decisions.choice: "[thịt] đã dâng tế" (L); "của tế lễ trong đền thần" (B); "đã được dâng cho thần" (R) for hierothyton
decisions.reason: The speaker uses a different, polite word from Paul's (m1), so the Vietnamese does not use the fixed phrase of 8:1-10:19 here.

decisions.choice: "제사에 바쳐진 [고기]" (L); "신전 제사에 쓴 고기" (B); "신에게 바친 것" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the speaker uses the polite word for sacrificial meat, not the word "offered to idols"; Korean keeps the difference, so the fixed phrase of chapter 8 is not used here.

source.text: συνείδησιν δὲ λέγω οὐχὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ ἑτέρου· ἱνατί γὰρ ἡ ἐλευθερία μου κρίνεται ὑπὸ ἄλλης συνειδήσεως;

records.literal_gloss: Conscience but I say not the of yourself but that of the other; why for the freedom of me is judged by another conscience?

en.L: Now I say conscience, not your own, but that of the other; for why is my freedom judged by another conscience?
en.B: By conscience I mean the other person's, not yours. For why should another person's conscience pass judgment on my freedom?
en.R: I mean the other person's conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by what someone else's conscience says?

fr.L: Or je dis la conscience, non la vôtre, mais celle de l’autre ; car pourquoi ma liberté est-elle jugée par une autre conscience ?
fr.B: Par conscience, j’entends celle de l’autre, et non la vôtre. Pourquoi, en effet, la conscience d’un autre jugerait-elle ma liberté ?
fr.R: Je parle de la conscience de l’autre, pas de la vôtre. Pourquoi ma liberté devrait-elle être jugée par ce que dit la conscience de quelqu’un d’autre ?

es.L: Ahora bien, digo conciencia, no la propia, sino la del otro; ¿pues por qué ha de ser juzgada mi libertad por otra conciencia?
es.B: Por conciencia me refiero a la del otro, no a la propia. Porque, ¿por qué ha de juzgar mi libertad la conciencia de otro?
es.R: Me refiero a la conciencia de la otra persona, no a la {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestra}}. ¿Por qué ha de juzgarse mi libertad por lo que dice la conciencia de otro?

sw.L: Lakini nasema dhamiri, si yako mwenyewe, bali ya yule mwingine; kwa maana kwa nini uhuru wangu uhukumiwe na dhamiri ya mwingine?
sw.B: Ninaposema dhamiri, ninamaanisha dhamiri ya mtu yule mwingine, si yako. Kwa maana kwa nini uhuru wangu uhukumiwe na dhamiri ya mtu mwingine?
sw.R: Ninamaanisha dhamiri ya mtu yule mwingine, si yako. Kwa nini uhuru wangu uhukumiwe kwa yale ambayo dhamiri ya mtu mwingine inasema?

vi.L: Nhưng tôi nói lương tâm, không phải của chính bạn, nhưng của người kia; vì sao sự tự do của tôi lại bị lương tâm người khác xét đoán?
vi.B: Khi nói đến lương tâm, tôi muốn nói lương tâm của người kia, không phải của bạn. Vì sao lương tâm của người khác lại xét đoán sự tự do của tôi?
vi.R: Tôi muốn nói đến lương tâm của người kia, không phải của bạn. Tại sao sự tự do của tôi lại bị xét đoán bởi những gì lương tâm của người khác nói?

ko.L: 내가 말하는 양심은 당신 자신의 [양심]이 아니라 다른 사람의 [양심]입니다. 왜 나의 자유가 다른 사람의 양심으로 판단을 받아야 합니까?
ko.B: 내가 말하는 양심은 당신의 양심이 아니라 그 다른 사람의 양심입니다. 왜 내 자유가 다른 사람의 양심에 따라 판단을 받아야 하겠습니까?
ko.R: 내가 말하는 것은 당신의 양심이 아니라 그 다른 사람의 양심입니다. 왜 내 자유가 다른 사람의 양심이 하는 말로 판단을 받아야 하겠습니까?

decisions.choice: whose conscience: the conscience of the one who informed, not the believer's own
decisions.reason: Paul explains verse 28. The believer refrains for the other's sake, not because his own conscience forbids the food.

decisions.choice: why is my freedom judged: Paul explains that his own freedom is not bound by another's conscience; he gives up eating only out of love
alternatives: an objection from a Corinthian, which Paul quotes
why give anyone the chance to condemn my freedom? that is, I refrain so as not to be condemned
decisions.reason: The question with γὰρ is hard to connect. Read with verse 28, it says that the believer does not change his own conviction: his freedom remains, and he holds it back only for the other person. Some read the question as a Corinthian protest that Paul answers in verses 31-33; others as Paul's reason for not giving offense. The words do not settle it.

decisions.choice: freedom: the believer's freedom to eat any food
decisions.reason: ἐλευθερία is the freedom Paul claimed for himself in 9:1, 19.

decisions.choice: By conscience I mean
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the explanation clear.

decisions.choice: no la propia
decisions.reason: The Greek reflexive points to the believer's own conscience in general. Spanish "la propia" says that without choosing a person; Readable says "la de ustedes", as the English Readable says "not yours".

source.text: εἰ ἐγὼ χάριτι μετέχω, τί βλασφημοῦμαι ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εὐχαριστῶ;

records.literal_gloss: If I with thanks partake, why am I slandered for that which I give thanks?

en.L: If I share [in the food] with thanks, why am I spoken evil of because of that for which I give thanks?
en.B: If I eat my share with gratitude, why should anyone speak evil of me over food for which I thank God?
en.R: I thank God for my food when I eat it. So why should anyone say bad things about me because of food I have thanked God for?

fr.L: Si moi, je prends part [à la nourriture] avec reconnaissance, pourquoi suis-je calomnié pour ce dont je rends grâce ?
fr.B: Si je mange ma part avec reconnaissance, pourquoi dirait-on du mal de moi à cause d’une nourriture pour laquelle je remercie Dieu ?
fr.R: Je remercie Dieu pour ma nourriture quand je la mange. Alors pourquoi quelqu’un dirait-il du mal de moi à cause d’une nourriture pour laquelle j’ai remercié Dieu ?

es.L: Si yo participo con gratitud, ¿por qué se habla mal de mí por aquello por lo que doy gracias?
es.B: Si como mi parte con gratitud, ¿por qué habría de hablar alguien mal de mí por una comida por la que doy gracias a Dios?
es.R: Doy gracias a Dios por mi comida cuando como. Entonces, ¿por qué alguien habría de hablar mal de mí por una comida por la que he dado gracias a Dios?

sw.L: Ikiwa mimi ninashiriki [chakula] kwa shukrani, kwa nini ninasemwa vibaya kwa ajili ya kile ninachokishukuru?
sw.B: Ikiwa ninakula sehemu yangu kwa shukrani, kwa nini mtu yeyote anisemee mabaya kwa sababu ya chakula ambacho nimemshukuru Mungu kwa ajili yake?
sw.R: Ninapokula chakula changu, ninamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili yake. Basi kwa nini mtu yeyote aseme mabaya juu yangu kwa sababu ya chakula ambacho nimemshukuru Mungu kwa ajili yake?

vi.L: Nếu tôi dự phần [thức ăn] với lòng biết ơn, sao tôi lại bị nói xấu vì thức ăn mà tôi đã tạ ơn?
vi.B: Nếu tôi ăn phần của mình với lòng biết ơn, sao lại có người nói xấu tôi về thức ăn mà tôi đã tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời?
vi.R: Tôi cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về thức ăn khi tôi ăn. Vậy tại sao có người lại nói xấu tôi vì thức ăn mà tôi đã cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời?

ko.L: 내가 감사함으로 [음식에] 참여한다면, 내가 감사하는 것 때문에 왜 비방을 받아야 합니까?
ko.B: 내가 감사하는 마음으로 내 몫을 먹는다면, 내가 하나님께 감사드리는 음식 때문에 왜 비난을 받아야 합니까?
ko.R: 나는 음식을 먹을 때 하나님께 감사드립니다. 그런데 내가 하나님께 감사드린 음식 때문에 왜 누가 나를 나쁘게 말해야 합니까?

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude to God for the food
decisions.reason: χάριτι usually means grace, but here it means thanks, as the verb εὐχαριστῶ, "I give thanks", shows. The same use is found in 15:57 and 2 Corinthians 2:14.

decisions.choice: spoken evil of: denounced, condemned by others
decisions.reason: βλασφημοῦμαι is to speak against someone, to slander. Someone who sees a believer eat sacrificial food might condemn him as an idolater.

decisions.choice: a second question, continuing verse 29
decisions.reason: It shares the uncertainty of verse 29 (29.s1, m2): it may express Paul's own freedom, which he holds back for others, or a protest he goes on to answer.

decisions.choice: thanks (L); gratitude (B); thank God (R)
decisions.reason: χάρις is a key term, normally "grace", but here the sense is thanks (m1).

decisions.choice: [in the food]
decisions.reason: The verb means to have a share in something; Literal supplies what is shared.

decisions.choice: participo, no brackets
decisions.reason: Spanish "participar" can stand alone for taking one's share at a meal, so Literal needs no bracketed "[in the food]".

decisions.choice: kwa shukrani
decisions.reason: Charis here is thanks to God for the food (meaning decision), so "shukrani", not the key term "neema" (grace).

decisions.choice: "감사함" (L); "감사하는 마음" (B); "하나님께 감사드리다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word usually translated "grace" here as thanks, as the verb "give thanks" in the same verse shows; Korean says "감사", not the key term "은혜".

source.text: Εἴτε οὖν ἐσθίετε εἴτε πίνετε εἴτε τι ποιεῖτε, πάντα εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ ποιεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: Whether then you eat or you drink or something you do, all things to glory of God do.

en.L: Whether, then, you eat or you drink or you do anything, do all things for [the] glory of God.
en.B: So then, when you eat, when you drink, whatever you do, do everything for God's glory.
en.R: So in everything you do, even in eating and drinking, live in a way that brings glory to God.

fr.L: Que vous mangiez donc, que vous buviez, ou que vous fassiez quoi que ce soit, faites toutes choses pour la gloire de Dieu.
fr.B: Ainsi, quand vous mangez, quand vous buvez, quoi que vous fassiez, faites tout pour la gloire de Dieu.
fr.R: Alors, dans tout ce que vous faites, même quand vous mangez et buvez, vivez d’une manière qui rend gloire à Dieu.

es.L: Así que, ya sea que {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}, o que {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}, o que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} cualquier cosa, {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}} todo para gloria de Dios.
es.B: Entonces, cuando {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}, cuando {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}, o cualquier cosa que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}}, {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}} todo para la gloria de Dios.
es.R: Así que en todo lo que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}}, incluso al comer y al beber, {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} de una manera que dé gloria a Dios.

sw.L: Basi, mkila au mkinywa au mkifanya jambo lolote, fanyeni yote kwa utukufu wa Mungu.
sw.B: Basi, mnapokula, mnapokunywa, chochote mnachofanya, fanyeni kila kitu kwa ajili ya utukufu wa Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo katika kila kitu mnachofanya, hata katika kula na kunywa, ishini kwa namna inayomletea Mungu utukufu.

vi.L: Vậy, dù anh chị em ăn, hay uống, hay làm điều gì, hãy làm mọi sự vì vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Vậy, khi anh chị em ăn, khi uống, hay làm bất cứ điều gì, hãy làm mọi việc vì vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Vậy trong mọi việc anh chị em làm, kể cả việc ăn uống, hãy sống sao cho đem vinh quang về cho Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러므로 여러분은 먹든지 마시든지 무엇을 하든지 모든 것을 하나님의 영광을 위하여 하십시오.
ko.B: 그러므로 먹을 때나 마실 때나, 무엇을 하든지 모든 일을 하나님의 영광을 위해 하십시오.
ko.R: 그러니 먹고 마시는 일까지 포함해서, 여러분이 하는 모든 일에서 하나님께 영광을 돌리는 삶을 사십시오.

decisions.choice: then: the conclusion of the whole discussion begun in 8:1
decisions.reason: οὖν gathers up chapters 8-10: the question of food is settled not by rules alone but by the aim of all one does.

decisions.choice: glory of God: God's greatness honored and made known
decisions.reason: δόξαν is God's own splendor, and to do something "for" it is to act so that he is honored and praised. Eating, drinking and every other act can do that.

decisions.choice: eating and drinking: the everyday acts this discussion has been about
decisions.reason: Paul starts from the food and drink in question and widens it to everything.

decisions.choice: even in eating and drinking; live in a way that
decisions.reason: Readable shows that ordinary acts are included, and puts "do" as a way of living.

source.text: ἀπρόσκοποι καὶ Ἰουδαίοις γίνεσθε καὶ Ἕλλησιν καὶ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, καθὼς κἀγὼ πάντα πᾶσιν ἀρέσκω, μὴ ζητῶν τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ σύμφορον ἀλλὰ τὸ τῶν πολλῶν, ἵνα σωθῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Without causing stumbling both to Jews become and to Greeks and to the church of the God, \v 33 as I also in all things all please, not seeking the of myself benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

en.L: Become people who cause no stumbling, both to Jews and to Greeks and to the church of God, \v 33 just as I also please everyone in everything, not seeking the benefit of myself but that of the many, in order that they may be saved.
en.B: Do not trip anyone up, not Jews, not Greeks, not the church of God. \v 33 I do the same: in all I do I seek to please all people, looking not for what helps me but for what helps the many, so that they may be saved.
en.R: Do not do anything that would make people fall into sin, whether they are Jews or people who are not Jews or members of God's church. \v 33 That is how I live. I try to please all people in all I do. I do not look for what is good for me. I look for what is good for many people, so that they will be saved.

fr.L: Devenez [des gens] qui ne font trébucher personne, ni les Juifs, ni les Grecs, ni l’Église de Dieu, \v 33 comme moi aussi je plais à tous en toutes choses, ne cherchant pas mon propre avantage, mais celui du grand nombre, afin qu’ils soient sauvés.
fr.B: Ne faites trébucher personne, ni les Juifs, ni les Grecs, ni l’Église de Dieu. \v 33 C’est ce que je fais moi-même : en tout ce que je fais, je cherche à plaire à tous, sans chercher ce qui m’est utile, mais ce qui est utile au plus grand nombre, pour qu’ils soient sauvés.
fr.R: Ne faites rien qui pourrait faire tomber quelqu’un dans le péché, que ce soient des Juifs, des non-Juifs ou des membres de l’Église de Dieu. \v 33 C’est comme cela que je vis. J’essaie de plaire à tout le monde dans tout ce que je fais. Je ne cherche pas ce qui est bon pour moi. Je cherche ce qui est bon pour beaucoup de gens, pour qu’ils soient sauvés.

es.L: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} tropiezo ni para judíos ni para griegos ni para la iglesia de Dios, \v 33 así como también yo agrado a todos en todo, no buscando mi propio beneficio sino el de los muchos, para que sean salvos.
es.B: No {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} tropezar a nadie: ni a judíos, ni a griegos, ni a la iglesia de Dios. \v 33 Yo hago lo mismo: en todo lo que hago procuro agradar a todos, y no busco lo que me beneficia a mí, sino lo que beneficia a los muchos, para que sean salvos.
es.R: No {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} nada que lleve a otros a caer en pecado, ya sean judíos, o personas que no son judías, o miembros de la iglesia de Dios. \v 33 Así vivo yo. Trato de agradar a todos en todo lo que hago. No busco lo que es bueno para mí. Busco lo que es bueno para mucha gente, para que se salven.

sw.L: Kuweni watu wasio kikwazo, kwa Wayahudi na kwa Wagiriki na kwa kanisa la Mungu, \v 33 kama vile mimi nami ninawapendeza wote katika mambo yote, nisitafute faida yangu mwenyewe bali ya wengi, ili waokolewe.
sw.B: Msimkwaze mtu yeyote, awe Myahudi, awe Mgiriki, au kanisa la Mungu. \v 33 Mimi nami hufanya vivyo hivyo: katika yote ninayofanya najitahidi kuwapendeza watu wote, nikitafuta si kile kinachonifaa mimi, bali kile kinachowafaa wengi, ili waokolewe.
sw.R: Msifanye jambo lolote litakalowafanya watu waanguke dhambini, wawe Wayahudi, watu wasio Wayahudi, au washiriki wa kanisa la Mungu. \v 33 Hivyo ndivyo ninavyoishi. Najitahidi kuwapendeza watu wote katika yote ninayofanya. Sitafuti kilicho chema kwangu. Natafuta kilicho chema kwa watu wengi, ili waokolewe.

vi.L: Hãy trở nên những người không gây vấp ngã cho người Do Thái, cho người Hy Lạp, và cho Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời, \v 33 cũng như tôi làm vừa lòng mọi người trong mọi sự, không tìm lợi ích cho riêng mình, nhưng cho nhiều người, để họ được cứu.
vi.B: Đừng làm ai vấp ngã, dù là người Do Thái, người Hy Lạp, hay Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 33 Tôi cũng làm như vậy: trong mọi việc tôi làm, tôi tìm cách làm vừa lòng mọi người, không tìm điều có lợi cho mình nhưng tìm điều có lợi cho nhiều người, để họ được cứu.
vi.R: Đừng làm điều gì khiến người khác sa vào tội lỗi, dù họ là người Do Thái, người không phải Do Thái, hay là thành viên Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 33 Tôi cũng sống như vậy. Tôi cố gắng làm vừa lòng mọi người trong mọi việc tôi làm. Tôi không tìm điều tốt cho mình. Tôi tìm điều tốt cho nhiều người, để họ được cứu.

ko.L: 유대인들에게도 그리스 사람들에게도 하나님의 교회에도 걸림이 되지 마십시오. \v 33 나도 모든 일에서 모든 사람을 기쁘게 하며, 나 자신의 유익을 구하지 않고 많은 사람의 유익을 구하는 것과 같이 [하십시오]. 그들이 구원을 받게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 유대인이든 그리스 사람이든 하나님의 교회든 아무도 넘어지게 하지 마십시오. \v 33 나도 그렇게 합니다. 나는 모든 일에서 모든 사람을 기쁘게 하려고 애쓰며, 나에게 유익한 것이 아니라 많은 사람에게 유익한 것을 찾습니다. 그들이 구원을 받게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 사람들을 넘어지게 해서 죄를 짓게 하는 일은 아무것도 하지 마십시오. 상대가 유대인이든 유대인이 아닌 사람이든 하나님의 교회의 교인이든 마찬가지입니다. \v 33 나도 그렇게 삽니다. 나는 무슨 일을 하든지 모든 사람을 기쁘게 하려고 애씁니다. 나에게 좋은 것을 찾지 않습니다. 많은 사람에게 좋은 것을 찾습니다. 그들이 구원을 받게 하려는 것입니다.

decisions.choice: causing no stumbling: giving no one a reason to fall into sin or turn away
decisions.reason: ἀπρόσκοποι can mean "blameless" (Philippians 1:10), but here it is set beside Jews, Greeks and the church as people who could be tripped up, so the active sense fits. It recalls the stumbling block of 8:9.

decisions.choice: Jews, Greeks and the church of God: everyone the believer has to do with
decisions.reason: Paul divides humanity into Jews and Greeks, that is, non-Jews (1:22-24), and adds the church, made up of both. Believers should not put an obstacle in the way of any of them.

decisions.choice: please: fit in with others for their good, not flatter them
decisions.reason: ἀρέσκω here means to serve the interests of others, as 9:19-22 describes; in Galatians 1:10 Paul refuses to please people in the sense of seeking their approval. The next words show the aim: their good, so that they may be saved.

decisions.choice: benefit ... of the many: what helps the many
decisions.reason: σύμφορον picks up the "benefit" of verse 23. "The many" is everyone else, as against Paul himself.

decisions.choice: that they may be saved: that they may come to faith and be kept in it to the end
decisions.reason: As in 9:22, Paul's purpose in giving up his rights is the salvation of others.

decisions.choice: Do not trip anyone up
decisions.reason: "Give offense" now suggests hurt feelings; the terms doc uses "trip up" for this stumbling picture.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: "Greeks" here means all non-Jews, as in 1:22-24; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: I do the same (B); That is how I live (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence at verse 33 and keep its link with verse 32.

decisions.choice: l'Église de Dieu, capitalised
decisions.reason: Set beside Jews and Greeks, the church here is God's people as a whole, not the one congregation at Corinth, so French uses the capital, as the style guide sets for the whole body of believers.

decisions.choice: tropiezo (L); hacer tropezar (B); llevar a caer en pecado (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:9 and 8:13: Literal keeps the noun "tropiezo", Balanced "hacer tropezar", and Readable says plainly what the fall is (m1).

decisions.choice: wasio kikwazo (L); msimkwaze (B)
decisions.reason: The "kikwazo / kukwaza" pair settled in 8:9-13, so this closing command echoes the stumbling block of chapter 8.
